meta.title: TU/e Digital Exhibition — WordPress & App Recap
meta.subtitle: Where the WordPress site and the new Nuxt application stand, what we are waiting for, and how the pieces fit together
meta.client: TU/e — Built Environment, Digital Exhibition platform
meta.author: marco@tech-paw.com
meta.scope: Staging / local only for now — nothing described here has been pushed to the live server.

tldr: The live WordPress site is unchanged apart from a few plugins added or removed. All the new work sits on staging / localhost. The plan is that after 6 November the current staging files will be merged with live.

The new front-end is a Nuxt application on Cloudflare. It reads pages from the WordPress REST API and shows them in a new layout, so WordPress stays the place where editors work. We still need to decide where the web app (Nuxt) is going to live.

Images come from one shared bucket for live, staging and the app (16.5 GB), instead of three copies. The staging uploads folder was deleted, so staging now relies only on the R2 bucket. For now, live keeps a duplicate of the uploaded images.

Before we go live we need: a decision on hosting (Cloudflare or somewhere else), approval of the latest staging, an email service, and testing of desktop, mobile and forms (most of these parts have already been tested). SEO is not a priority, but we will check which analytics and tracking tools we have or need.

actions.title: Email system
actions.detail: Password reset and the contact form need a working mail service. Brevo is the proposed option (free plan: 300 emails per day) as an alternative to Microsoft Graph via Azure. WP Mail SMTP on WordPress and the contact endpoint in the app both connect to it.
actions.ask: Choose Brevo or Microsoft Graph, so the sender domain can be set up.

actions.title: To investigate: analytics & tracking
actions.detail: SEO is not a priority. What we do want to know is which of these tools the site has today, or needs: Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Google Tag Manager and a cookie script.
actions.ask: Find out which of these are in use today and which are wanted.

actions.title: Approve the latest staging website
actions.detail: Staging was updated after the last meeting (notes of 2026-10-29 and the back-end and front-end changes up to 1 November). It now has: the renamed theme, media served only from the R2 bucket, a site-settings endpoint the app reads for logos, menus and footer, a Deploy Frontend button that follows the build until it is live, and video support in the media library. The staging and production databases are not synchronised, but both are up to date.
actions.ask: Log in to the latest staging, review it and confirm, so the merge after 6 November can go ahead.

actions.title: Decide the hosting
actions.detail: Where the web application (Nuxt on Cloudflare) and the bucket (R2?) will live. Jonathan suggests Bunny.net.
actions.ask: Decide the hosting for the app and the bucket.

actions.title: Merge staging and turn it into production
actions.detail: The live site has barely changed (a few plugins added or removed). The files and the database of staging will be merged into live, unless more content is added in the meantime.
actions.ask: Planned after 6 November, once staging is approved (A3) and the hosting is decided (A4).

actions.title: Tests before going live
actions.detail: Most parts have already been tested. Once the WordPress live site has been updated, the application gets a final check on desktop and mobile, including the forms. On WordPress, the new admin UX/UI gets manual and automated testing.
actions.ask: Manual and automated testing of the new WordPress interface, after WordPress live is live.

postmortem.title: Post-mortem — the theme update that broke the front-end
postmortem.summary: WordPress updated the site's theme by itself and replaced our files with a different theme. That broke the layout of the WordPress site. We renamed the theme, so it is no longer connected to the WordPress theme repository and this cannot happen again. The theme is now called tue-digital-exhibition, a name that does not exist in the WordPress repository (not automatic download anymore).

chain.label: Automatic update
chain.text: WordPress updated the theme on its own.

chain.label: Files replaced
chain.text: The theme had no child theme, so the update replaced it completely with files from the WordPress theme repository.

chain.label: Layout broken
chain.text: The WordPress front-end design stopped working.

chain.label: Theme renamed
chain.text: The theme is now called tue-digital-exhibition, which is not in the WordPress theme repository, so no update can overwrite it.

changesIntro: The live site still has its current content, with only a few plugins added or removed. Staging has had several changes. The files and the database of staging will be merged into the live website, unless more content is added in the meantime.

discovery.summary: Within the hosting platform (Flask) we found a web application firewall. Sometimes it made the deployment of the app hard, because it blocked requests that our development and deployment need.

modes.label: Staging
modes.text: The firewall is on and blocks what it considers a risk. This is the setting that got in our way.

modes.label: Live website
modes.text: The firewall only records what it would block. It blocks nothing.

discovery.did: For development we added security rule ID 210580 to the firewall settings, so that it no longer blocks our work.
discovery.optionsTitle: The three ways to handle it

options.title: Keep the exception
options.text: The firewall stays on and rule 210580 is added to its settings. This is what we do now.

options.title: Switch it off
options.text: The firewall stops filtering requests altogether.

options.title: Detection only
options.text: Like the live website: it records suspicious requests but never blocks them.
